goal: Improve the active Taro gear-slot hierarchy with a smaller slot label, a larger item name, backend-derived secondary-stat labels, and top-right confirmed enhancement-state markers.
userValue: Players can scan each equipped item and understand its slot, identity, secondary attributes, and confirmed gem/enchant/embellishment state without opening the editor.
nonGoals: Do not change target-only outer geometry, the eight route regions, the sixteen-slot grid, or the locked outer-page scroll contract.
Do not change server, PostgreSQL, public payloads, typed API, Resolver ownership, enhancement legality, or candidate application semantics.
Do not infer secondary stats, eligibility, or configured enhancements from candidates, craftedStatOptions, modCapabilities, or local drafts.

currentTruth.factOwner: The backend gear read model owns item attributes and the canonical Resolver owns confirmed selectedOptions; Taro derives display-only labels from those returned facts.

mustChange: The gear-detail presentation model must expose backend-derived secondary-stat labels and confirmed enhancement state per equipped slot.
GearSlotWorkbench and its styles must render the requested information hierarchy without changing interaction ownership.
The current gear-detail truth and component contracts must record the display boundary.
mustNotChange: server/, PostgreSQL, public payloads, typed API and canonical Resolver remain unchanged.
Candidate/variant application and enhancement confirmation remain explicit draft-to-Resolve flows.
The legacy pages/builds/detail.js and unrelated project configuration remain unchanged.
riskUnknown: A long item name and multiple labels may compete with the fixed row height and the top-right state markers.
Initial read-model rows may not carry enough data to assert enhancement eligibility; neutral markers must not claim an applicable slot.
evidenceRequired: Targeted model and page-contract Vitest coverage for secondary-stat and confirmed-enhancement presentation.
UI architecture audit, typecheck and WeChat build on the final candidate head.
Exact candidate-head WeChat smoke and user acceptance for gear_slot_information_hierarchy and gear_slot_enhancement_state.

ownership.factOwner: Backend item facts and Resolver selectedOptions remain authoritative; the active Taro route and GearSlotWorkbench only render their confirmed display projection.

engineeringHealth.reason: The change stays in existing frontend presentation owners, adds no request, write path or new fact source, and uses code rollback.

acceptanceEvidence: Targeted Vitest proves that slot labels contain only backend-derived secondary attributes and that enhancement markers use confirmed selections only.
The UI architecture audit, typecheck and WeChat build verify the active Taro owners and final candidate package.
The user verifies the exact candidate build in WeChat DevTools for information hierarchy and confirmed enhancement-state markers.

decisionLog.decision: The user confirmed that equipped slot rows should prioritize a smaller slot label, larger item name, real secondary attributes and top-right confirmed enhancement state without changing canonical gear behavior.
